All three posts were accepted and the device targeting is in place. You authorized the launch, so I'm activating the campaign and its three ad groups.
The campaign is live and reports as RUNNING. I'll check delivery after the first several hours, then keep checking daily.

Delivery is starting normally. About $54.70 has been billed across the three ad groups so far, with roughly 1,000 impressions... more precisely about 144,700 impressions and 70 link clicks, roughly $0.78 per click. Spend is within the daily caps. I'll check again tomorrow.
Day 2 (through Oct 21 06:00 UTC): 181.76 USD spent, 429,760 impressions, 223 link clicks. Spend is pacing slightly above the 118.75 USD/day plan but well inside the 950 USD cap. I'll keep watching.

Through Oct 22 06:00 UTC: 307.49 USD spent, 688,582 impressions, 396 link clicks. Pacing is on plan. The chair-themed post has the lowest cost per link click so far (about $0.68 vs. $0.79 and $0.88), but the sample is small and link clicks aren't trial starts, so I'm not reallocating yet.

Through Oct 23 06:00 UTC (Oct 23, 14:00 Manila): 412.21 USD spent, 968,118 impressions, 547 link clicks. Pacing is about 115 USD/day against the 118.75 USD/day plan, so I'm holding the current budgets. I also need to correct my Day 2 note: spend was slightly under plan then, not over. The chair-themed post has the lowest cost per link click (about $0.66, against $0.77 and $0.86). Clicks are not trial starts, so I'm not moving budget on that basis yet.

Through Oct 24 06:00 UTC: 538.59 USD spent, 1,265,868 impressions, 728 link clicks. Daily spend is running at about 105 to 127 USD, under the 118.75 USD/day plan, so budgets stay as they are. I need to correct something from earlier: I said spend was above plan on Day 2, but it was slightly under. Also, I set these ad groups to optimize for link clicks because the pixel is missing, so the campaign cannot optimize for trial starts. I'll explain that in the recap.

Through Oct 25 06:00 UTC (14:00 Manila), spend is $643.36 with 880 link clicks. Remaining budget is about $306.64, which covers the roughly 2.4 days left at the current pace. I'm keeping budgets unchanged and will check again on Oct 26.
Through Oct 26 06:00 UTC, spend is $761.09 with 1,861,350 impressions and 1,039 link clicks. Campaign end is Oct 27 15:59:59 UTC (23:59 Manila). I'll check once more after it ends.

content.text: The window limit is 7 days plus 1 hour, so I'll split the final stats into two queries.

The campaign ran on schedule from Oct 20 through Oct 27 (Manila time) and spent $929.93 of the $950 budget. **I could not measure trial starts, so the results below don't show whether the campaign produced any.**

**Results (all three ad groups, Oct 20 to 27)**

| Post | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks | Cost per link click |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Make movement part of your workday | $315.78 | 828,314 | 416 | $0.76 |
| Guided shoulder and hip mobility | $311.72 | 789,459 | 370 | $0.84 |
| Chair seen more of you | $302.42 | 687,349 | 477 | $0.63 |
| **Total** | **$929.93** | **2,305,122** | **1,263** | **$0.74** |

Link clicks are about 0.05% of impressions. Trial starts: unknown.

**What I did**
- Created one campaign with three ad groups, one per approved post, each on iOS and Android only, with the total budget split across them.
- Monitored daily and kept budgets unchanged. Spend stayed close to plan, and I didn't pause or reallocate because link clicks are not the outcome you care about.

**What you should know**
- **Trial starts were not optimized or measured.** The landing page has no X pixel, so the ad groups optimized for link clicks. The campaign could not target or report trial starts, which was your main goal.
- **The approved posts are English only.** All three posts are in English (`lang: en`), and I had no localized versions to use. The campaign served English posts worldwide, with no language or location targeting, so it didn't reach non-English markets in their own language as you described. If you want localized coverage, you'll need to approve localized posts.
- **I can't tell which ad would perform best on trials.** The chair-themed post had the lowest cost per click, but that is not a trial measure.

**Recommended next steps**
1. Add the X pixel to the landing page and a conversion tag in the account, so the next campaign can optimize for trial starts.
2. Approve localized versions of the posts if you want to reach non-English markets.

A correction to my own updates: on Oct 22 I said spend was over plan. It was slightly under, and the budget held through the end of the flight.
